name: T-connection without junction dot
summary: A conductor meeting another at a right angle and stopping there, which IEC practice reads as a connection even without a dot.
description: In IEC drawing practice a conductor that runs into another and ends there forms a T-connection, and the connection is understood whether or not a dot is drawn. Many drafting standards still recommend the dot for clarity, but undotted tees are common on legacy and vendor drawings.

The convention depends on the drawing family. On some ANSI-style drawings an undotted tee may be ambiguous, which is why a dot is preferred there. Readers should check the drawing legend. A T-connection only shows electrical continuity; it does not tell you where the physical joint is, which may be at a terminal some distance away.
readingNotes: Check the legend to see whether undotted tees are used as connections.
Find the physical terminal or joint that realises the tee.
drawingChecklist: Apply one tee convention consistently across the set.
Prefer a dot where drawings may be read under other conventions.
Avoid four-way crossings that rely on dots alone.
distinction: An undotted tee is a connection; a plain four-way crossing without a dot is normally read as no connection.
